source.author: hor
source.text: Fingit equum tenera docilem cervice magister ire viam qua monstret eques; venaticus, ex quo tempore cervinam pellem latravit in aula, militat in silvis catulus, nunc adhibe puro pectore verba puer, nunc te melioribus offer, quo semel est imbuta recens, servabit odorem testa diu.
source.text_original: Fingit equum tenera docilem cervice magister / ire viam qua monstret eques; venaticus, ex quo  / tempore cervinam pellem latravit in aula, / militat in silvis catulus, nunc adhibe puro / pectore verba puer, nunc te melioribus offer, / quo semel est imbuta recens, servabit odorem / testa diu.
source.text_english: The trainer teaches the horse, with its supple neck, to go along the road the rider shows; the hunting pup, from the time it barked at the deer-skin in the hall, serves in the woods. Now address words to the boy’s pure breast; now present yourself to one better, for the vessel will long keep the scent it once took on when fresh.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: rudis testa diu et saporem retinet et odorem, quo primum imbuta est.
reuse.text_original: rudis testa diu et saporem retinet et odorem, quo primum imbuta est.
reuse.text_english: A rough earthen vessel long retains both the taste and the smell with which it was first imbued.
